dimensions.assessment: Affects children under 14 whose Social Security cards are compromised via loss or theft during mailing, along with their parents or guardians.
dimensions.evidence: a child who has not attained the age of 14... in the course of transmission of a social security card to the child, the confidentiality of such number has been compromised

dimensions.assessment: Provides a new Social Security number to prevent identity compromise for affected young children.
dimensions.evidence: the Commissioner shall issue a new social security account number to such child

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative processing changes by the Social Security Administration without specified appropriation amounts.
Amends a specific section of the Social Security Act to add a narrow reissuance pathway.
dimensions.evidence: Section 205(c)(2)(B) of the Social Security Act (42 U.S.C. 405(c)(2)(B)) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent statutory requirement taking effect 180 days after enactment.
dimensions.evidence: The amendments made by subsection (a) shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of the enactment of this Act.

missing_information: Estimated number of children affected annually and administrative cost to the Social Security Administration.
importance_detail.rationale: Directs the Social Security Administration to issue a new Social Security number to young children under 14 whose initial cards were lost or stolen in the mail.
